annotation.summary_en: Two Nazi officers interrogate various partisans during the war, but the officer orders an immediate execution the moment he encounters an Armenian prisoner.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: The sketch takes place in a wood-paneled office designed as a Nazi-parody interrogation room, complete with swastika armbands, an officer cap, and a portrait on the wall. Two Nazi officers sit at a desk discussing good news from the front lines, stating their troops have advanced another 50 kilometers. They decide to get to work interrogating captured partisans. The first prisoner, a Russian, is brought in and interrogated briefly before being sent off. The second, a Ukrainian named Nikol Gavrilov, is ordered to be shot immediately. Finally, a third prisoner wearing a striped shirt is brought in. When he identifies himself as Armenian ('Armyan'), the lead officer panics and screams to have him shot instantly without a single question. When his subordinate asks why they aren't interrogating the Armenian like the others, the officer explains the practical danger: if you start talking to an Armenian and ask a couple of questions, it will inevitably turn out that you are either acquaintances or long-lost relatives, making it impossible to finish the job.
